claims.claim: A registered public key may issue credentials
Two root key IDs necessarily represent two independent authorities
A predecessor chain alone prevents offline rollback
A local file anchor protects rollback of both bundle and anchor storage
Rotation, targeted revocation, offline import and single-store rollback detection are locally exercised
Time-effective key revocation can preserve valid historical evidence while blocking later trust

reproducedFailures.failure: a merely registered key could self-issue reviewer/provider credentials
reproducedFailures.repair: pinned-root issuer grants bounded by kind, tenant, scope, validity and exact digest

reproducedFailures.claim: two root keys imply independent control
reproducedFailures.failure: multiple keys could belong to one custodian
reproducedFailures.repair: threshold counts distinct externally pinned custodian IDs

reproducedFailures.claim: revoked issuer cannot create later credentials
reproducedFailures.failure: backdated issuedAt could bypass revocation without sovereign acceptance time
reproducedFailures.repair: credential checked at declared issuance and sovereign acceptance time

reproducedFailures.failure: disk attacker can replace the whole signed bundle with an earlier bundle
reproducedFailures.repair: independent local anchor detects bundle-store rollback; joint rollback remains explicitly unqualified

reproducedFailures.failure: crash after bundle write before anchor advance could leave fail-closed but manually stranded state
reproducedFailures.repair: pending journal distinguishes interrupted phases and recovers only an unambiguous verified transition

reproducedFailures.failure: immediate revocation erased verification of valid historical evidence
reproducedFailures.repair: effective-time verifyAt preserves prior evidence and blocks later trust

reproducedFailures.failure: archive policy and self-test still emitted version 31
reproducedFailures.repair: archive build, verification and self-test are now bound to version 32

reproducedFailures.failure: nested runner and shared result file could hang after complete TAP output
reproducedFailures.repair: direct Node TAP runs, separate logs and hashes, no shared result file or force-exit

limitations: Signatures prove authorization and material binding, not truth or legal independence.
The independent file anchor detects rollback of the bundle store alone; joint rollback of bundle and anchor remains unprotected without external monotonic storage, HSM or federation.
The proof is single-host and uses local test keys; PostgreSQL, KMS/HSM, live provider and human value are not qualified.
Root custodian organization identities are configured locally and are not independently or legally verified.
The stability harness change is locally exercised; long-duration cross-platform flake probability remains unknown.
nextAction: External qualification of roots, custodians, revocation propagation, monotonic witnessing, PostgreSQL, KMS/HSM, isolation, security and human value.
